reporting-org.narrative: Organisation des Nations unies pour l'éducation, la science et la culture (UNESCO)
United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

description.narrative:
The biennium workplan for basic sciences that involves institutional and human capacity building and advocacy in the field of basic sciences.
The basic sciences constitute the core of modern science, and they are, and will be, at the root of any innovative science answer to meet basic human needs and solve pressing challenges of sustainable development. From quality science education at all academic levels, to building institutional research capacity, to promoting and catalyzing international scientific collaboration and networks, to facilitating access to scientific information in particular through open science and open access to scientific information, UNESCO’s work in capacity development is at the heart of its mandate in science. UNESCO will therefore continue to implement its capacity-building mandate in the sciences through the following:
Objectives: • In this biennium, we will expand two promising initiatives that were successfully launched in the previous biennium ‘Providing Scientists with Remote Access to Scientific Laboratory Equipment’ and ‘Series of science entrepreneurship boot camps’. We aim to cover more Member States and train more researchers. Our objective is to provide African scientists and scientists from Global South access to sophisticated equipment unavailable in their institutions.
• The International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development (IDSSD) has been proclaimed in August 2023. The decade will run from 2024-2033. All activities performed in this work plan will be under the umbrella of the IDSSD. Our objective is to highlight the role of science in resolving global challenges and getting all Member States involved.
• The International Basic Sciences Programme (IBSP) fosters interregional collaboration and promote research and training hubs of scientific excellence in the basic sciences, with special emphasis on Africa. These scientific programmes and hubs have proven to be an efficient means of strengthening institutional and human capacity in the basic sciences in the Member States, and will be mobilized to provide and develop new research and training opportunities for young scientists, with a focus on girls and women. International Basic Sciences Programme (IBSP) recommendations shall guide action in this area and shall help in promoting demand/development driven in the basic sciences, with special emphasis on Africa and SIDS.
Following up on extrabudgetary projects related to Basic Sciences.
Key activities:
- Providing remote access to X-Ray diffractometer for African scientists and expanding the initiative to include other techniques and geographical regions - Holding an entrepreneurship boot camp for basic sciences researchers - Reconstitution of the new IBSP board and holding the IBSP statutory meeting - Capacity building activities (training and workshops) for scientists from Global South - Conducting a series of webinars to educate researchers. The webinars will be mainly held during the celebration of International days. - Initiating and finalizing new partnerships that would help us implement our goals and achieve ambitious results and real impact in the new biennium. - Holding the 'Rebuilding Scientific Infrastructure in Ukraine' symposium to support recovery of scientific infrastructure
Deliverables: - Train at least 25 researchers - Provide remote access to at least 3 new Member States - Hold 2 webinars
